title: COVID-19 and the Loss of Rituals, Formation of New Ones with Michael Norton, PhD

sentences.en: Almost daily,
sentences.zh: 几乎每天，

sentences.en: the news is full of stories of high school and college seniors missing out on their graduation ceremonies and of people being unable to see and touch their loved ones who are suffering from COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 新闻里都充斥着高中生和大学生错过毕业典礼，以及人们无法探视和接触受新冠疫情折磨的亲人的报道。

sentences.en: Some of the more heartbreaking accounts feature families having to bury loved ones without funerals or formal mourning.
sentences.zh: 一些更令人心碎的叙述中，家庭成员不得不埋葬亲人，却无法举行葬礼或进行正式的哀悼。

sentences.en: The coronavirus is keeping us from experiencing some of the deepest and most meaningful rituals of our lives.
sentences.zh: 新冠病毒让我们无法体验生活中一些最深刻、最有意义的仪式。

sentences.en: What is this doing to us psychologically?
sentences.zh: 这对我们的心理有什么影响？

sentences.en: How important are rituals to our mental health and well-being?
sentences.zh: 仪式对我们的心理健康和幸福感有多重要？

sentences.en: What new rituals might we be creating?
sentences.zh: 我们可能会创造出哪些新的仪式？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探索心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Michael I.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是迈克尔·I·诺顿博士，

sentences.en: Norton, a professor of business administration at the Harvard Business School and a member of Harvard's Behavioral Insights Group.
sentences.zh: 他是哈佛商学院的工商管理教授，也是哈佛大学行为洞察小组的成员。

sentences.en: His research covers a gamut of fascinating topics from money to daydreaming, from greed to deception.
sentences.zh: 他的研究涵盖了从金钱到白日梦，从贪婪到欺骗等一系列引人入胜的话题。

sentences.en: But I asked him here today to talk primarily about rituals in light of the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 但我今天请他来，主要是为了谈谈新冠疫情背景下的仪式。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, Dr. Norton.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》，诺顿博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for inviting me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: I think we probably all have an idea of what rituals are, but it always helps to have a common language.
sentences.zh: 我想我们大概都知道什么是仪式，但拥有共同的语言总是有帮助的。

sentences.en: Is it, for example, a ritual to take a coffee break every day at 10.15, or is that just a habit?
sentences.zh: 例如，每天10点15分休息喝咖啡是仪式，还是仅仅是一种习惯？

sentences.en: What are the differences between rituals and habits?
sentences.zh: 仪式和习惯之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Could you define for our listeners what constitutes a ritual?
sentences.zh: 您能为我们的听众定义一下什么是仪式吗？

sentences.en: There certainly lie in a continuum.
sentences.zh: 它们确实处于一个连续体上。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of habits that have some ritualistic elements, and there are a lot of rituals that, of course, look a lot like habits.
sentences.zh: 所以，有很多习惯带有某种仪式感，当然，也有很多仪式看起来非常像习惯。

sentences.en: So it's hard to differentiate them into pure, that's purely a habit, and that's purely a ritual.
sentences.zh: 因此，很难将它们完全区分开来，说这是纯粹的习惯，那是纯粹的仪式。

sentences.en: But one way to think about that continuum is, if I ask you in the morning, do you first brush your teeth and then take a shower?
sentences.zh: 但思考这个连续体的一种方法是，如果我早上问你，你是先刷牙还是先洗澡？

sentences.en: Or do you first take a shower and then brush your teeth?
sentences.zh: 或者你是先洗澡还是先刷牙？

sentences.en: It's, crazily, when I ask that question, in countries all over the world, actually, about 50% of people do it one way, and 50% of people do it the other way.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的是，当我问这个问题时，在世界各地的国家，大约50%的人会这样做，而另外50%的人会那样做。

sentences.en: So they have this thing they do every morning, and they really think their way is the good way, and the other way is the bad way.
sentences.zh: 所以他们每天早上都会做这件事，而且他们真的认为自己的方式是好的，而另一种方式是坏的。

sentences.en: Now, then if I ask, imagine in your head, and you can do this yourself, imagine in your head doing them in the opposite order tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果我让你想象一下，你也可以自己试着想象一下，明天早上以相反的顺序做这些事。

sentences.en: Like, really simulate that you would, instead of brushing your teeth first, you'd get in the shower firSt.
sentences.zh: 比如，真正模拟一下，你不是先刷牙，而是先去洗澡。

sentences.en: When I ask people that, a lot of people make a face, like, I don't like that, that feels weird to me, or that feels wrong to me.
sentences.zh: 当我问人们这个问题时，很多人会皱起眉头，好像在说，我不喜欢那样，那让我感觉很奇怪，或者那让我感觉不对劲。

sentences.en: But a lot of people say, no problem at all, I'm happy to switch the order.
sentences.zh: 但也有很多人说，没问题，我很乐意切换顺序。

sentences.en: You can see in there sort of the difference between a habit and a ritual.
sentences.zh: 你可以从中看出习惯和仪式之间的区别。

sentences.en: So if you like to do things a certain way, but then if I say switch it, you don't mind, it's more like a habit.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你喜欢以某种方式做事，但如果我让你换一下，你并不介意，那更像是一种习惯。

sentences.en: In the morning, you need to brush your teeth, you need to take a shower, you have a habit of doing that, the order doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 早上，你需要刷牙，需要洗澡，你习惯这样做，顺序其实并不重要。

sentences.en: But if you're one of those people who felt a little weird when you thought about doing it differently, now that's a little bit further down the continuum toward a ritual.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是那些想到要以不同方式做这件事时感到有点奇怪的人之一，那么这就更接近仪式了。

sentences.en: Because now the order in which you do things really matters to you.
sentences.zh: 因为现在你做事的顺序对你来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: When it really shouldn't matter necessarily, it feels like it matters, and that means that it's a little bit more important to you.
sentences.zh: 当它本来不一定非要重要时，它却感觉很重要，这意味着它对你来说更重要一些。

sentences.en: So rituals seem to be ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 所以仪式似乎无处不在。

sentences.en: I mean, I can't think of a culture or a time in history when humans did not engage in rituals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想不出人类在历史上哪个文化或时期不参与仪式。

sentences.en: They can seem trivial, like buying a weekly lottery ticket, or they can be really profound, like a funeral mass.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来可能微不足道，比如每周买一张彩票，或者它们可能非常深刻，比如葬礼弥撒。

sentences.en: So my question is, are we physically hardwired to perform rituals?
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，我们天生就注定要进行仪式吗？

sentences.en: What does the science tell us about where this drive comes from?
sentences.zh: 科学告诉我们这种驱动力来自哪里？

sentences.en: One of the interesting things about studying rituals is, of course, that many different disciplines have tackled the topic.
sentences.zh: 研究仪式的一个有趣之处在于，许多不同的学科都探讨过这个话题。

sentences.en: I'm certainly not the first person to start studying rituals.
sentences.zh: 我当然不是第一个开始研究仪式的人。

sentences.en: So if you look in anthropology and sociology, of course, in clinical psychology, which I hope we'll talk about as well,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看人类学和社会学，当然还有临床心理学，我希望我们也能谈谈这一点，

sentences.en: people have been looking at what rituals are and how ubiquitous they are.
sentences.zh: 人们一直在研究什么是仪式以及它们有多普遍。

sentences.en: And in fact, if you think about how we identify that some humans had some culture way back when, we often look to see if they buried their dead in a ceremonious fashion or not.
sentences.zh: 事实上，如果你思考我们是如何确定某些人类在很久以前就有了某种文化的，我们通常会观察他们是否以仪式化的方式埋葬死者。

sentences.en: So if they don't, then we say maybe they didn't have culture in a sense.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们没有这样做，那么我们可能会说他们某种意义上没有文化。

sentences.en: But when there's shells around the body, we use that to say they must have felt differently about death.
sentences.zh: 但当尸体周围有贝壳时，我们就会用它来说明他们对死亡一定有不同的感受。

sentences.en: They must have had beliefs about death.
sentences.zh: 他们一定对死亡有某种信仰。

sentences.en: They must have wanted to honor that person as a group.
sentences.zh: 他们一定想作为一个群体来纪念那个人。

sentences.en: So rituals, in a way, are one of the ways we identify when humans became human.
sentences.zh: 所以，仪式在某种程度上是我们识别人类何时成为人类的方式之一。

sentences.en: So sheltering in place and needing to keep at least six feet away from most other people are actions that have radically altered our lives and prevented us from doing so many things.
sentences.zh: 因此，居家隔离和需要与大多数人保持至少六英尺的距离，这些行动彻底改变了我们的生活，并阻止了我们做许多事情。

sentences.en: What's the long-term impact of missing out on some of the rituals I mentioned earlier, especially not being able to fully grieve loved ones we've lost to the coronavirus?
sentences.zh: 错过我之前提到的某些仪式，特别是无法充分哀悼我们因新冠病毒而失去的亲人，会有什么长期影响？

sentences.en: I think our research would suggest that there is good news and bad news.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们的研究表明有好消息也有坏消息。

sentences.en: So one of the first projects that we did on rituals, I did with my colleague Francesca Gino on grieving rituals.
sentences.zh: 我们做的关于仪式的第一个项目之一，是我和我的同事弗朗西斯卡·吉诺一起做的关于哀悼仪式的研究。

sentences.en: And one of the things we saw is we sort of thought we would be studying grief in terms of the public communal rituals we all think of, often religious rituals as well.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的一件事是，我们原以为会从我们都想到的公共集体仪式，通常也是宗教仪式的角度来研究悲伤。

sentences.en: But when we asked people, you know, think of someone who you loved who passed away, and we asked them just, what did you do after that?
sentences.zh: 但当我们问人们，你知道，想想你爱过但去世的人，我们只是问他们，在那之后你做了什么？

sentences.en: Many people wrote something like, well, there was a funeral, but then they would write something very private that they did just for that person, just by themselves,
sentences.zh: 许多人写道，嗯，有葬礼，但随后他们会写下一些他们只为那个人做的、非常私人的事情，只是他们自己做的，

sentences.en: that often no one else even knew about.
sentences.zh: 通常甚至没有其他人知道。

sentences.en: One of the examples that always stays with me is an older woman whose husband had passed away, and she wrote, I washed his car every week as he used to.
sentences.zh: 其中一个总是让我印象深刻的例子是一位丈夫去世的老妇人，她写道，我每周都像他过去那样洗他的车。

sentences.en: Now, that's clearly not an established public ritual that's thousands of years old.
sentences.zh: 现在，这显然不是一个有几千年历史的既定公共仪式。

sentences.en: Cars don't even exist until fairly recently.
sentences.zh: 汽车直到最近才出现。

sentences.en: So we know that that woman made that ritual up herself.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道那位女士是自己编造了那个仪式。

sentences.en: But as you listen to it, you can see how meaningful and important it was to her.
sentences.zh: 但当你听的时候，你可以看出这对她来说是多么有意义和重要。

sentences.en: And what we find in our research, and this is the good news, is that even those private ones that we make up ourselves, those are associated with less grief and better coping.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中发现，这是好消息，即使是我们自己编造的那些私人仪式，也与更少的悲伤和更好的应对方式有关。

sentences.en: Now, that's not to say that the communal ones aren't incredibly important because we need social support.
sentences.zh: 现在，这并不是说公共仪式不重要，因为我们需要社会支持。

sentences.en: We need all kinds of things to get through grief.
sentences.zh: 我们需要各种各样的东西来度过悲伤。

sentences.en: And that's the bad news, that losing those really does have an impact.
sentences.zh: 这就是坏消息，失去这些确实会产生影响。

sentences.en: The good news is we can have a little bit of flexibility in creating our own, and those can help, too.
sentences.zh: 好消息是我们可以在创造自己的仪式方面有一点灵活性，这些仪式也能有所帮助。

sentences.en: One of the rituals that you've studied is the simple handshake.
sentences.zh: 你研究过的仪式之一是简单的握手。

sentences.en: That's something else that we can't engage in right now.
sentences.zh: 那是我们现在无法进行的其他事情。

sentences.en: Even Dr. Anthony Fauci has suggested, maybe facetiously, that we may never shake hands again.
sentences.zh: 甚至安东尼·福奇博士也曾暗示，也许是开玩笑，我们可能再也不会握手了。

sentences.en: Do you think that's the case?
sentences.zh: 你认为会这样吗？

sentences.en: And can you talk about some of the types of communication that are inherent in handshaking, why it's so important?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈握手中固有的某些交流类型，以及为什么它如此重要吗？

sentences.en: In research that was led by Julianna Schroeder, who's at Berkeley, we tried to look to see what really handshakes are all about.
sentences.zh: 在朱莉安娜·施罗德（在伯克利）领导的研究中，我们试图看看握手到底是怎么回事。

sentences.en: In fact, there's, I think it's apocryphal, unfortunately, but there is a story that the reason handshakes began way back when is because by shaking hands,
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个故事，不幸的是，我认为它是杜撰的，但有一个故事说握手之所以在很久以前就开始了，是因为通过握手，

sentences.en: you would dislodge any daggers from your sleeves and they would fall on the ground.
sentences.zh: 你可以抖掉袖子里的任何匕首，它们就会掉在地上。

sentences.en: So you would know you could trust the person.
sentences.zh: 这样你就知道你可以信任那个人了。

sentences.en: That's probably not true, but if you think about the psychological element there, it's really showing that you can trust me,
sentences.zh: 那可能不是真的，但如果你考虑其中的心理因素，它确实表明你可以信任我，

sentences.en: that we can be close enough to each other to touch and nobody's going to get killed.
sentences.zh: 我们可以足够亲近地接触，而且没有人会被杀。

sentences.en: So handshakes are a sign of truSt.
sentences.zh: 所以握手是信任的标志。

sentences.en: Now, that's exactly what we see in our research, actually, is that when people shake hands, they tend to trust each other more.
sentences.zh: 现在，这正是我们在研究中看到的，实际上，当人们握手时，他们往往更信任彼此。

sentences.en: The reason is that by shaking hands, I'm signaling that I care about you and that you can trust me back.
sentences.zh: 原因是，通过握手，我是在发出信号，表明我在乎你，你可以反过来信任我。

sentences.en: That's the bad news, because as you said, we can't shake hands right now, and who knows if we'll get back to that ritual.
sentences.zh: 这是坏消息，因为正如你所说，我们现在不能握手，谁知道我们是否会回到那种仪式。

sentences.en: But the good news is that it's not really the handshake itself that matters.
sentences.zh: 但好消息是，真正重要的并不是握手本身。

sentences.en: It's the ability to communicate that you care about someone else and that you trust them.
sentences.zh: 而是能够传达你关心别人并且信任他们的能力。

sentences.en: And we ran a study, and this is years ago before the current crisis, where we had someone refuse to shake hands with somebody else.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了一项研究，这是在当前危机发生几年前，我们让一个人拒绝与另一个人握手。

sentences.en: And in general, people think the person's a jerk.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，人们认为那个人是个混蛋。

sentences.en: But if the person says, hey, the reason I'm not shaking your hand is because I've had a cold.
sentences.zh: 但如果那个人说，嘿，我不和你握手的原因是因为我感冒了。

sentences.en: Well, now suddenly the person who shakes hands is a jerk because they're giving you a cold.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在突然间，握手的人成了混蛋，因为他们在传染给你感冒。

sentences.en: And the person who doesn't, by not shaking your hand, is showing they care about you and they can trust you.
sentences.zh: 而不握手的人，通过不和你握手，表明他们在乎你，并且他们可以信任你。

sentences.en: So again, I think we have, even though handshakes are so ubiquitous, we do have some flexibility in how we try to accomplish the goal that handshakes were doing.
sentences.zh: 所以再次强调，我认为我们有，尽管握手非常普遍，但我们在尝试实现握手所能达到的目标方面确实有一些灵活性。

sentences.en: And again, we can be a little bit freelancing on to figure out how we can actually signal those things.
sentences.zh: 同样，我们可以稍微自由发挥，找出我们如何能够真正发出这些信号。

sentences.en: Quite a few athletes engage in some peculiar behaviors during or before games.
sentences.zh: 不少运动员在比赛期间或比赛前会进行一些奇怪的行为。

sentences.en: For example, you noted in an article in Scientific American that Wade Boggs, the former third baseman for the Boston Red Sox, woke up exactly at the same time each day,
sentences.zh: 例如，你在《科学美国人》的一篇文章中指出，前波士顿红袜队三垒手韦德·博格斯每天都在同一时间醒来，

sentences.en: ate chicken before each game, took precisely 117 ground balls in practice, took batting practice at 517, and ran sprints at 717.
sentences.zh: 每场比赛前吃鸡肉，练习时精确地接117个地滚球，5点17分进行击球练习，7点17分进行短跑。

sentences.en: Is that kind of behavior a little crazy or does it serve an important purpose?
sentences.zh: 这种行为是有点疯狂，还是它有重要的目的？

sentences.en: One of my favorite things about that, I'm from Boston.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，我最喜欢的事情之一是，我来自波士顿。

sentences.en: Wade Boggs played for the Boston Red Sox.
sentences.zh: 韦德·博格斯曾为波士顿红袜队效力。

sentences.en: He also used to, at every bat, he would write the Hebrew word for life in the dirt.
sentences.zh: 他过去在每次击球时，都会在泥土上写下希伯来语的“生命”一词。

sentences.en: And the best part of that is that he wasn't Jewish,
sentences.zh: 最棒的部分是，他不是犹太人，

sentences.en: so he just decided that he would adopt something from another religion that seemed to be pretty good and then bring it into his performance.
sentences.zh: 所以他只是决定采用另一种宗教中看起来相当不错的东西，然后把它带入他的表现中。

sentences.en: Yeah, we do see these performance rituals that are so ubiquitous.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们确实看到了这些如此普遍的表现仪式。

sentences.en: And when athletes do them, they can be incredibly elaborate.
sentences.zh: 当运动员进行这些仪式时，它们可能极其复杂。

sentences.en: And we think they're a little unusual, but we don't really think it's a problem.
sentences.zh: 我们认为它们有点不寻常，但我们并不认为这是一个问题。

sentences.en: So Rafael Nadal has a very elaborate pre-serve ritual that he does every time.
sentences.zh: 所以拉斐尔·纳达尔每次都有一个非常复杂的发球前仪式。

sentences.en: And if you ask these players, why do you do it, they'll say, it's a ritual and it helps me perform better.
sentences.zh: 如果你问这些球员，你为什么要这样做，他们会说，这是一种仪式，它能帮助我表现得更好。

sentences.en: So they're doing it on purpose to try to accomplish this goal.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是有意这样做，试图实现这个目标。

sentences.en: Sometimes I think if I did one of those crazy rituals, like before I taught a class, I'd be fired because nobody thinks that teaching is as hard as playing tennis.
sentences.zh: 有时我想，如果我做了其中一个疯狂的仪式，比如在我教课之前，我会被解雇，因为没有人认为教书像打网球那么难。

sentences.en: So we have context-specific rituals that we're allowed to do and not allowed to do.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有允许做和不允许做的特定情境仪式。

sentences.en: But even for mundane things like people like us who aren't playing professional sports, but we have to teach or lead a meeting or give a presentation that we're worried about,
sentences.zh: 但即使对于像我们这样不从事职业体育运动的人来说，我们必须教书、主持会议或进行我们担心的演讲，

sentences.en: Allison Woodbrooks, another colleague of mine at HBS, led this project on do rituals help calm us down in those situations?
sentences.zh: 我在哈佛商学院的另一位同事艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯领导了这个项目，研究仪式是否有助于我们在这些情况下冷静下来？

sentences.en: And the answer is that they do, actually.
sentences.zh: 答案是，它们确实有帮助。

sentences.en: So when we're feeling anxious, the worst thing to do is tell yourself to calm down.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们感到焦虑时，最糟糕的事情就是告诉自己冷静下来。

sentences.en: And by the way, that's the most important takeaway, maybe, is the whole thing is never try to tell yourself just to calm down.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这可能是最重要的收获，整件事就是永远不要试图告诉自己冷静下来。

sentences.en: We just can't do it.
sentences.zh: 我们就是做不到。

sentences.en: But doing a little ritual before we perform actually can calm us down a little bit and then help us perform a little bit better.
sentences.zh: 但在我们表现之前做一个小仪式实际上可以让我们冷静一点，然后帮助我们表现得更好一点。

sentences.en: I've seen videos that you've done on the internet where you have people do these rituals to demonstrate group cohesion.
sentences.zh: 我看过你在互联网上做的视频，你让人们做这些仪式来展示群体凝聚力。

sentences.en: And so I think you have found that they do that.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你已经发现它们确实做到了这一点。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, people who are excluded from those rituals become an out group because they are excluded from the rituals.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，被排除在这些仪式之外的人会成为外群体，因为他们被排除在仪式之外。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just sort of a peculiar thing that we tend to do even without thinking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是一种我们即使不思考也倾向于做的奇怪事情。

sentences.en: And you talk about group cohesion and the importance of rituals, what they do for the people who are in the groups and how they maybe harm the people who are out.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了群体凝聚力和仪式的重要性，它们对群体内的人有什么作用，以及它们可能如何伤害群体外的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is one of the paradoxes of rituals is that they're not just good.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是仪式的悖论之一，它们不仅仅是好的。

sentences.en: And of course, we know that because rituals taken too far can become a symptom of obsessive compulsive disorder, which we know isn't good.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道这一点，因为仪式做得太过分可能会成为强迫症的症状，我们知道这不好。

sentences.en: So we know that it's not just that more rituals is better.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道并不是仪式越多越好。

sentences.en: And I would never want anyone to think that what I'm saying is more rituals is better.
sentences.zh: 我绝不希望任何人认为我所说的是仪式越多越好。

sentences.en: They have to be used when it's appropriate.
sentences.zh: 它们必须在适当的时候使用。

sentences.en: But another way that they're not good for us as well is you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 但它们对我们不利的另一种方式是，你是完全正确的。

sentences.en: They bond us together, but in the bonding us together, they can drive us apart from other people.
sentences.zh: 它们把我们联系在一起，但在把我们联系在一起的过程中，它们可能会把我们与其他人分开。

sentences.en: When I talk about this, I do have people stand up and perform a ritual in groups.
sentences.zh: 当我谈到这一点时，我确实会让人们站起来，分组进行仪式。

sentences.en: And I made it up.
sentences.zh: 而且是我编造的。

sentences.en: So I just I say, here's something I made up.
sentences.zh: 所以我只是说，这是我编造的东西。

sentences.en: Can we all do it together?
sentences.zh: 我们能一起做吗？

sentences.en: And it's things like clapping and stomping your hands and things like that.
sentences.zh: 比如拍手和跺脚之类的动作。

sentences.en: And all I say to the group is go ahead.
sentences.zh: 我对小组说的只是开始吧。

sentences.en: And what happens is people start the ritual and they very quickly get in sync so that everyone starts clapping at the same time and then stomping at the same time.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是人们开始仪式，他们很快就同步了，每个人都开始同时拍手，然后同时跺脚。

sentences.en: And they really like it.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: They feel good about each other.
sentences.zh: 他们对彼此感觉很好。

sentences.en: They're looking around smiling.
sentences.zh: 他们环顾四周，微笑着。

sentences.en: It's like, this is our ritual.
sentences.zh: 就像，这是我们的仪式。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: But you also see that if someone, quote unquote, messes up, meaning that I clap instead of stomp at the wrong time, people get very angry at the person.
sentences.zh: 但你也会看到，如果有人，引用引号，搞砸了，意思是说我在错误的时间拍手而不是跺脚，人们会对那个人非常生气。

sentences.en: So they look at them, you know, what's wrong with you?
sentences.zh: 所以他们看着他们，你知道，你怎么了？

sentences.en: And when I ask them at the end, what did you think about those people?
sentences.zh: 当我在最后问他们，你们对那些人有什么看法时？

sentences.en: They say, well, you know, he was doing it wrong.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，你知道，他做错了。

sentences.en: Now, remember, I told them I just made up this ritual that they've never done before.
sentences.zh: 现在，记住，我告诉过他们我只是编造了这个他们以前从未做过的仪式。

sentences.en: There's no wrong.
sentences.zh: 没有错。

sentences.en: There's no right.
sentences.zh: 没有对。

sentences.en: I just made it up.
sentences.zh: 我只是编造了它。

sentences.en: I told them I just made it up.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过他们我只是编造了它。

sentences.en: And yet immediately, that quickly, we can say this is the good way.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却能立刻、迅速地断定这就是正确的方法。

sentences.en: We do it this way.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这样做的。

sentences.en: And if you do it the other way, I don't like you.
sentences.zh: 如果你用别的方法，我就不喜欢你了。

sentences.en: And we do see that in two separate projects.
sentences.zh: 我们在两个独立的项目中确实看到了这一点。

sentences.en: So with Tammy Kim, we showed that rituals can bond us together.
sentences.zh: 在与塔米·金（Tammy Kim）的合作中，我们展示了仪式如何将我们凝聚在一起。

sentences.en: And with Nick Hobson, we showed actually that rituals can drive us apart in exactly this way.
sentences.zh: 而在与尼克·霍布森（Nick Hobson）的合作中，我们恰恰展示了仪式如何以这种方式将我们分离开来。

sentences.en: So let's talk for a minute about rituals and clothing.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们花点时间谈谈仪式与服装。

sentences.en: A lot of us have spent the last couple, almost two months in sweatpants or pajamas most of the day.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人在过去几个月，几乎是两个月的时间里，大部分时间都穿着运动裤或睡衣。

sentences.en: And a popular meme on social media asks, when was the last time you wore pants with buttons?
sentences.zh: 社交媒体上有一个流行的梗问道：你上一次穿带扣子的裤子是什么时候？

sentences.en: So I think we know that clothing has meaning in pretty much every culture.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都知道，在几乎每种文化中，服装都有其含义。

sentences.en: What are some of the actual rituals surrounding clothing and how do they affect us psychologically?
sentences.zh: 围绕服装的实际仪式有哪些？它们在心理上是如何影响我们的？

sentences.en: One of the very first things we did when we started studying rituals was we asked research assistants to find every grieving ritual that any human group had ever enacted in human history.
sentences.zh: 我们开始研究仪式时做的第一件事，就是要求研究助理找出人类历史上任何人类群体曾经实施过的所有哀悼仪式。

sentences.en: So that was their task, and we set them loose.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们的任务，我们让他们放手去做。

sentences.en: And pretty much every recorded culture has a grieving ritual.
sentences.zh: 几乎每一种有记载的文化都有哀悼仪式。

sentences.en: It's something that often has communal elements.
sentences.zh: 这通常包含群体性的元素。

sentences.en: And we know this.
sentences.zh: 我们对此心知肚明。

sentences.en: Whatever culture you're in, you know exactly the one in your culture.
sentences.zh: 无论你身处哪种文化，你都清楚地知道自己文化中的那种仪式。

sentences.en: One of the things that we found in that research is color plays an extremely important role in grieving, but it's not very consistent from culture to culture.
sentences.zh: 我们在研究中发现的一点是，颜色在哀悼中起着极其重要的作用，但不同文化之间的差异很大，并不统一。

sentences.en: So many, many cultures, of course, have black as the color associated with grief.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多许多文化都将黑色与哀悼联系在一起。

sentences.en: You wear black to the funeral, etc.
sentences.zh: 比如参加葬礼时要穿黑色衣服等等。

sentences.en: Other colors, though, have white.
sentences.zh: 然而，其他文化则以白色为主。

sentences.en: That's the color that is associated with grief.
sentences.zh: 那是与哀悼相关的颜色。

sentences.en: If you wore black to that funeral, people would be furious at you.
sentences.zh: 如果你在那种葬礼上穿黑色，人们会因为你的行为而感到愤怒。

sentences.en: If you wore white to a funeral where black is the appropriate color, those people would be furious at you.
sentences.zh: 如果你在应该穿黑色的葬礼上穿白色，人们也会对你感到愤怒。

sentences.en: There's other cultures where red or green are associated with grief as well.
sentences.zh: 还有一些文化将红色或绿色与哀悼联系在一起。

sentences.en: So it's really interesting to me in this way because it's clear that people want to use color to help cope with their grief, and they use the color of their clothing in particular.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说非常有趣，因为很明显，人们希望利用颜色来帮助应对悲伤，尤其是通过服装的颜色。

sentences.en: But then there's a little bit of flexibility on exactly which color you end up using.
sentences.zh: 但对于最终使用哪种颜色，其实有一定的灵活性。

sentences.en: I think the good thing about wearing colors that we really lost is that we used to be able to signal to other people where we were in our process of grief.
sentences.zh: 我认为穿上我们已经失去的颜色，其好处在于我们过去能够向他人传达我们处于哀悼过程的哪个阶段。

sentences.en: When people wore black for a year, for example, you would know that they'd lost someone, and that might help you support them.
sentences.zh: 例如，当人们穿一年黑衣时，你会知道他们失去了亲人，这或许能帮助你给予他们支持。

sentences.en: Now, of course, many cultures have gotten rid of those grieving rituals.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在许多文化已经摒弃了这些哀悼仪式。

sentences.en: So when I meet someone, I don't know if they've lost a loved one yesterday or a year before or never.
sentences.zh: 所以当我遇到某人时，我不知道他们是昨天失去了亲人，还是在一年前，亦或是从未有过。

sentences.en: So it changes my ability to support them.
sentences.zh: 这改变了我支持他们的能力。

sentences.en: The plus side is, of course, now not everyone knows my business, and I might be a private person.
sentences.zh: 当然，好处是现在不是每个人都知道我的私事，而且我可能是一个注重隐私的人。

sentences.en: So there's these trade-offs between giving up rituals to get us some things, but we also often lose some things along the way.
sentences.zh: 因此，放弃仪式以换取某些东西是有代价的，但我们往往也会在过程中失去一些东西。

sentences.en: Are there still some cultures where you have to wear a color for, say, a year?
sentences.zh: 是否还有一些文化要求你必须穿某种颜色的衣服，比如持续一年？

sentences.en: I know in my family, which was Italian, which is Italian, that you were supposed to wear black for a year if you were a widow.
sentences.zh: 我知道在我的意大利裔家庭中，如果身为遗孀，是需要穿一年黑衣的。

sentences.en: Is that still prevalent?
sentences.zh: 这种情况现在还普遍吗？

sentences.en: Some cultures do.
sentences.zh: 有些文化确实如此。

sentences.en: Speaking of professional sports, you'll see sports teams often wear a black armband for a season if someone important to the sports franchise passes away.
sentences.zh: 说到职业体育，你会看到如果体育界的某个重要人物去世，运动队通常会佩戴一个赛季的黑色臂章。

sentences.en: So we still see people using clothing in order to signal something important.
sentences.zh: 所以我们仍然看到人们利用服装来传达重要的信息。

sentences.en: But the variability from culture to culture and even within culture and subculture is very wide in terms of exactly what people do to show that they're grieving over time.
sentences.zh: 但是，就人们随着时间推移如何表达哀悼而言，不同文化之间，甚至在同一文化和亚文化内部，其差异性都非常大。

sentences.en: Something else a lot of us are also experiencing during our physical distancing is not being able to get our hair cut or doing it ourselves or having someone we live with do the job.
sentences.zh: 我们在保持物理距离期间经历的另一件事是，无法理发，或者不得不自己动手，又或是让同住的人帮忙。

sentences.en: When does caring for our hair move from being just a habit, I get my hair cut every month, or an actual ritual?
sentences.zh: 打理头发何时从一种习惯（比如我每个月理一次发）变成了一种真正的仪式？

sentences.en: This is a hard one for me to answer because I'm bald.
sentences.zh: 这个问题对我来说很难回答，因为我是秃头。

sentences.en: I don't have a lot of these.
sentences.zh: 我没有多少头发。

sentences.en: Sadly, I don't have this problem.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，我没有这个烦恼。

sentences.en: But even here we see, even speaking just within grief again, there we see again that people often do something with hair when they're grieving.
sentences.zh: 但即使在这里，我们也能看到，仅就哀悼而言，人们在悲伤时往往会对头发做些什么。

sentences.en: But it varies extremely widely, again, from culture to culture.
sentences.zh: 但同样，不同文化之间的差异极大。

sentences.en: So in some cultures, you shave your head when someone passes away.
sentences.zh: 在某些文化中，当有人去世时，你会剃光头。

sentences.en: In other cultures, you grow your beard when someone passes away.
sentences.zh: 在其他文化中，你会留起胡须。

sentences.en: In other cultures, you take a snippet of the person's hair and keep it like in a locket to honor them.
sentences.zh: 在另一些文化中，你会剪下一缕逝者的头发，放在吊坠里以示纪念。

sentences.en: And so even within the domain of specifically hair, again, it seems like just with color, it seems like people want to do something to honor that loss.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使在头发这个领域，就像颜色一样，人们似乎都想做点什么来纪念那种失去。

sentences.en: They look around for what's available.
sentences.zh: 他们会环顾四周，看看有什么可用的。

sentences.en: It might be clothing.
sentences.zh: 可能是服装。

sentences.en: It might be their own bodies.
sentences.zh: 可能是他们自己的身体。

sentences.en: And then they do something in order to try to enact a ritual to help them and to help others cope with that loss.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会采取行动，试图通过仪式来帮助自己和他人应对那种失去。

sentences.en: Another obsession for some of us during the pandemic lockdown is food.
sentences.zh: 疫情封锁期间，我们一些人的另一个执念是食物。

sentences.en: We're cooking at home more.
sentences.zh: 我们在家做饭的时间更多了。

sentences.en: A lot of people are baking or starting sourdough starters, which brings to mind food rituals.
sentences.zh: 很多人在烘焙或开始制作酸种面团，这让人想到了饮食仪式。

sentences.en: And I know you've also looked at those.
sentences.zh: 我知道你也研究过这些。

sentences.en: I'm wondering about some rituals such as saying grace before dinner or having a sommelier go through a whole elaborate ceremony and pouring wine.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇一些仪式，比如晚餐前的餐前祷告，或者让侍酒师进行一套繁琐的仪式来斟酒。

sentences.en: Does this make food somehow better for us?
sentences.zh: 这会让食物对我们来说变得更美味吗？

sentences.en: Bizarrely enough, it seems to.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: So in research led by Kathleen Voss, we actually look to see does performing rituals around food actually make the food taste better?
sentences.zh: 在凯瑟琳·沃斯（Kathleen Voss）领导的一项研究中，我们确实观察了围绕食物进行的仪式是否真的能让食物尝起来更美味。

sentences.en: Should it taste better?
sentences.zh: 它应该尝起来更好吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不会。

sentences.en: You know, the way you prepare something doesn't necessarily mean it will taste better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，准备食物的方式并不一定意味着它会更好吃。

sentences.en: But when people prepare and consume food ritualistically, we can show that they actually enjoy the experience more.
sentences.zh: 但当人们以仪式化的方式准备和食用食物时，我们可以证明他们实际上更享受这个过程。

sentences.en: Very simplest one is we gave people free chocolate.
sentences.zh: 最简单的一个例子是，我们给了人们免费的巧克力。

sentences.en: And some people we just said, go ahead and eat it.
sentences.zh: 对一些人，我们只是说，吃吧。

sentences.en: And other people we said things like, first break it in half, then unwrap that half, then eat that half, then unwrap the other half.
sentences.zh: 而对另一些人，我们说：先把它掰成两半，然后拆开那一半的包装，吃掉那一半，再拆开另一半的包装。

sentences.en: You know, not very complicated, but still an orderly progression through eating the chocolate, a little bit ritualistic.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这并不复杂，但吃巧克力的过程是有序的，带有一点仪式感。

sentences.en: And we find that people like eating the chocolate more, in part because when you do a ritual around food, it immerses you much more in the experience.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们更喜欢吃巧克力，部分原因在于当你围绕食物进行仪式时，它会让你更沉浸在体验中。

sentences.en: So think typically about eating food.
sentences.zh: 想想平时吃东西的时候。

sentences.en: You might be on your phone.
sentences.zh: 你可能在看手机。

sentences.en: You might be watching TV.
sentences.zh: 你可能在看电视。

sentences.en: You might be distracted.
sentences.zh: 你可能分心了。

sentences.en: You're not really engaged in the consumption act.
sentences.zh: 你并没有真正投入到进食的行为中。

sentences.en: Rituals seem to bring us into the act so that we end up savoring the food more.
sentences.zh: 仪式似乎把我们带入了当下，让我们最终能更细细品味食物。

sentences.en: We're literally leaving the chocolate in our mouth longer and enjoying it more because it's sort of focused our attention on what we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们确实把巧克力在嘴里含得更久，也更享受它，因为仪式集中了我们对正在做的事情的注意力。

sentences.en: Are there any rituals you would recommend that our listeners engage in right now so that they can feel more in control and less stressed?
sentences.zh: 你有什么建议的仪式可以让我们的听众现在就开始参与，从而让他们感到更有掌控感、压力更小吗？

sentences.en: In a project that we have just started since this crisis, my student Jimena Garcia-Rada is leading this.
sentences.zh: 在我们自这场危机开始以来刚刚启动的一个项目中，我的学生吉梅娜·加西亚-拉达（Jimena Garcia-Rada）正在领导这项工作。

sentences.en: We've surveyed parents and asked them about Jimena studies decision-making in couples, which is a fascinating topic in its own right.
sentences.zh: 我们调查了父母，询问他们关于……吉梅娜研究的是夫妻决策，这本身就是一个迷人的课题。

sentences.en: But we've looked to see what's happened to parenting during the crisis because almost everyone's parenting has changed in very different ways, but there's been change.
sentences.zh: 但我们观察了危机期间育儿发生了什么变化，因为几乎每个人的育儿方式都以非常不同的方式发生了改变，但确实发生了变化。

sentences.en: So we ask people a very simple question.
sentences.zh: 所以我们问了人们一个非常简单的问题。

sentences.en: Have you created any new rituals as a parent with your kids since the crisis began?
sentences.zh: 自危机开始以来，作为父母，你和孩子之间是否创造了任何新的仪式？

sentences.en: A huge number of people have, I think 50 to 60% say that they have, and those parents tend to feel a little better about their parenting,
sentences.zh: 有很大一部分人表示有，我想有50%到60%的人说他们有，而这些父母对自己的育儿方式感觉更好一些，

sentences.en: and they're a little bit happier with their lives in general.
sentences.zh: 他们对自己的生活总体上也更满意一些。

sentences.en: Now, it's obviously possible that people who are happy with their parenting have the time to create rituals, so we don't know the causal direction in this case.
sentences.zh: 当然，对育儿方式感到满意的父母可能有时间去创造仪式，所以我们不知道这种情况下的因果方向。

sentences.en: But it does seem as though when the world gives us uncertainty, we tend to look to rituals as a way to cope with the uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 但当世界给我们带来不确定性时，我们似乎确实倾向于寻求仪式作为应对不确定性的方式。

sentences.en: So parents are doing rituals around hand-washing.
sentences.zh: 所以父母们正在围绕洗手进行仪式。

sentences.en: They're doing rituals around wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 他们正在围绕戴口罩进行仪式。

sentences.en: They're helping their kids through the process of learning how to do that, just like the way we do at bedtime or at mealtimes with our kids,
sentences.zh: 他们正在帮助孩子学习如何做到这一点，就像我们平时在睡前或用餐时对待孩子那样，

sentences.en: where you have to have this particular bunny and then this story, and then we sit over there, and then mommy comes in.
sentences.zh: 比如必须要有这只特定的兔子，然后讲这个故事，然后我们坐在那边，然后妈妈进来。

sentences.en: You know, we have this whole elaborate thing for kids that we do all the time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们总是为孩子做这一整套繁琐的事情。

sentences.en: Parents use rituals like crazy.
sentences.zh: 父母们非常频繁地使用仪式。

sentences.en: Then for some reason, we think when we're grown up, well, those are silly.
sentences.zh: 然后出于某种原因，我们认为当我们长大后，那些都是愚蠢的。

sentences.en: We don't need them.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要它们。

sentences.en: Well, maybe if they work for kids, they might work for us, too.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许如果它们对孩子有效，对我们可能也有效。

sentences.en: So we're going to be singing happy birthday as we wash our hands for the rest of our lives, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们余生洗手时都要唱《生日快乐歌》，对吧？

sentences.en: I bet people, it's almost like an earworm.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，这几乎就像一种“耳虫”效应。

sentences.en: I bet people will have it way more in their head now as they're washing than they ever did before.
sentences.zh: 我敢说，人们现在洗手时脑子里浮现出这首歌的频率比以前高多了。

sentences.en: Well, Dr. Norton, thank you so much for joining Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 好的，诺顿博士，非常感谢您参加《心理学谈话》（Speaking of Psychology）。

sentences.en: This has been really interesting, and I hope our listeners have learned a lot from hearing about your research.
sentences.zh: 这真的非常有趣，我希望我们的听众从您的研究中获益良多。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: And to our listeners, thank you for tuning into our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 也感谢我们的听众收听我们的播客。

sentences.en: This is one of the series we have produced regarding psychology's role in helping us understand and navigate the COVID-19 pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这是我们制作的关于心理学在帮助我们理解和应对新冠疫情方面所起作用的系列节目之一。

sentences.en: You can find other resources and tip sheets about coping through the pandemic on our website at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 您可以在我们的网站 APA.org 上找到关于应对疫情的其他资源和提示单。

sentences.en: You can also find previous episodes of Speaking of Psychology on Apple, Stitcher, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 您也可以在 Apple、Stitcher、YouTube 或任何您获取播客的地方找到《心理学谈话》之前的剧集。

sentences.en: All episodes are available on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: 所有剧集都可以在我们的网站 www.speakingofpsychology.org 上找到。

sentences.en: If you have comments or ideas for future podcasts, email us at speakingofpsychology at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 如果您有评论或对未来播客的想法，请发送电子邮件至 speakingofpsychology@APA.org。

sentences.en: That's Speaking of Psychology, all one word, at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 即 Speaking of Psychology，全部连在一起，后面接 @APA.org。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: For the American Psychological Association, I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 代表美国心理学会，我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
